Version 1.7.0 of the specification: 54 change requests and 0 defects are recorded beside it, 0 items open. Open items come first, then the ones carried out, then the ones closed without a change. ### CR-1: Make meta-model 1.0.0 the first stable version of every SpecArch format

Raised by specification-author on 2026-10-25, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact major. Status: released.

Authors need a format that does not move under them. Meta-model 1.0.0 promises that no key is renamed, moved, removed or made required, and that no meaning changes, for the whole 1.x; before freezing it, two keys of 0.3 that each meant two things are renamed.

Cause: changed (the need changed after it was written).

Affects: changes SA-95.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-10-25. A stable format is what lets a specification outlive the release it was written with; every earlier version stays read beside 1.0.0, and specarch upgrade moves a file, so nothing written before is lost (ADR-186).

Released in 1.0.0.

### CR-6: Keep each proposal for the specification as an idea record with its status, decision and what it became, checked by the validator and named by specarch decision why and rests

A proposal raised in a conversation, a table, an example or a review was lost once taken or turned down, so a reader of a decision could not see the idea it came from, nor an author the ideas still open; the specification needs each one kept beside it as a record, checked, and named on the decision it became.

The idea kind is one more kind in the 1.0 record schema and two rules (idea_decision, idea_question), and validate, decision why and decision rests read records/ideas/ beside the specification as well. specarch diff calls those three commands' change major, since each change is the description of an entry of their reads, a list whose items have no name, and the rule for such a list is cautious on purpose so that a person decides. Raised by specification-author on 2026-10-28, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

A call's send and receive expressions could be read but not checked on real values, so an author could not see what a request would carry or what a record would keep before the code was written, and a mistake in a mapping showed only at the integration test.

### CR-14: Let decide answer a question that blocks a decision with a record that rests on it, not with origin decided

Raised by specification-author on 2026-10-29, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact patch. Status: released.

decide told the author to mark a blocked decision with origin decided and decidedIn, which validate refuses with origin_decision, so following its line made the specification invalid (BUG-065).

### CR-27: Settle the acceptance loop: record a remark from acceptance with its build, place and cause, answer it by a decision, keep the approval's commit and show what an open change reaches

Raised by specification-author on 2026-10-31, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

Affects: adds `#/decisions/ADR-221`, `#/decisions/ADR-223`, `#/decisions/ADR-224`, `#/stakeholders/owner`, `#/sources/owner-review-2026-10-31`, `#/tests/diff-same-version`, `#/tests/document-writes-changes-reach`, `#/tests/validate-acceptance-record`, `#/tests/validate-acceptance-valid`, `#/tests/validate-change-answered`; changes `#/decisions/ADR-083`, `#/requirements/SA-57`, `#/commands/approve`, `#/commands/diff`, `#/commands/document`.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-04. The record schema 1.0 now requires cause on a change that is analysed, approved, rejected, implemented or released (ADR-223, the owner's decision of 2026-10-31), so a 1.0 change record in one of those states written without cause is an error that 1.4.0 did not give; the fix is one key per record. The owner decided on 2026-11-04 to release that as 1.5.0. Every other addition is optional: phase acceptance, against, seenAt, observed, expected and questions; the approval's commit, written by approve with a line on standard error when the folder has changes not committed; diff leaving the version check out between two folders of one version; document reading the change records to show what an open change reaches. So apart from cause, no file clean on 1.4.0 gets a new error, and a minor release carries it (ADR-186, ADR-083).

Released in 1.5.0.

Affects: adds `#/decisions/ADR-236`, `#/requirements/SA-130`, `#/tests/diff-lists-transition`, `#/tests/document-changes-transition`, `#/tests/generate-bpmn-as-is`, `#/tests/generate-bpmn-to-be`, `#/tests/validate-workflow-as-is`, `#/tests/validate-workflow-as-is-refused`; changes `#/commands/diff`, `#/commands/document`, `#/commands/generate`.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-04. A workflow takes an optional asIs, in the workflow's shape without asIs; the workflow's own keys stay the to-be. Both validators check the as-is by the workflow's rules at its own pointer, the changes document writes a section Transitions and specarch diff a transition line per part, every generator gets the to-be, and specarch generate --as-is gives the as-is in its place (ADR-236, SA-130). The diff's standard output gains transition lines only for a workflow that keeps an as-is, a key no 1.4.0 file has, and --as-is is a new option, so no file clean on 1.4.0 gets a new error, a new output line or a new exit status, and a minor release carries it (ADR-186, ADR-083).

Released in 1.5.0.

A system delivered to a customer is accepted in the customer's environment by people who have neither the project's code nor its test harness; they could only check the specification's golden, red and uncovered paths by hand, in a spreadsheet the specification never saw again.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-04. specarch generate tests --package <environment> writes one file, specarch-test-package.yaml, every test and every derived case no test covers as a request to that environment's servers, holding no credential; specarch run runs it from outside and writes JUnit XML that log test-run maps back, a derived case to its subject's element (ADR-233, SA-128). --package is a new option and run a new command, and log test-run is itself new since 1.4.0 (ADR-230), so no file clean on 1.4.0 gets a new error, a new output line or a new exit status, and a minor release carries it (ADR-186, ADR-083).

### CR-40: Read existing test scripts and test sheets into tests with extract tests, and keep them in merge

Raised by specification-author on 2026-11-04, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-04. specarch extract tests reads Gherkin feature files and CSV, TSV or Excel test sheets into tests inferred from them, each citing where it was read, with a must question for each test's subject and for each given, step or expected result the script leaves out; merge keeps a test that cites a source of its tree, and the questions that block only such tests (ADR-235, SA-131). tests is a new extract source, and merge keeps only tests no 1.4.0 tree could hold, so no file clean on 1.4.0 gets a new error, a new output line or a new exit status, and a minor release carries it (ADR-186, ADR-083).

Raised by specification-author on 2026-11-04, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

A team delivering from a specification is asked every week how big it is, what is still open and who must answer, whether every role was heard, what the change requests cost and how far the delivery has come; nothing counted these in one place, and no record held the effort a change request took, so the figures lived in a tracker that drifts from the specification.

Cause: omitted (the specification left it out).

Affects: adds `#/decisions/ADR-237`, `#/requirements/SA-132`, `#/tests/document-progress-effort-not-counted`, `#/tests/document-progress-for-everyone`, `#/tests/document-progress-stakeholders-held`, `#/tests/document-progress-uncounted-entries`, `#/tests/document-writes-progress`, `#/tests/validate-change-effort`; changes `#/commands/document`, `#/commands/validate`.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-04. specarch document progress writes progress.md from the specification and the records beside it: the size by stage and section, the open questions by priority and deciding role, the unheard roles, the stakeholder list's confirmation, the effort each change request records with the ones that record none named as missing, and a burn-up per release; a change record takes an optional effort with estimatedHours and spentHours, and nothing is estimated where nobody recorded a figure (ADR-237, SA-132). progress is a new document target and effort a new optional key, so no file clean on 1.4.0 gets a new error, a new output line or a new exit status, and a minor release carries it (ADR-186, ADR-083).

### CR-42: Propose a reservation made outside the branches for each sequential ID, so parallel branches stop landing the same decision and requirement numbers

Raised by specification-author on 2026-11-04, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact patch. Status: released.

When several branches of one specification are written at once, each takes the largest decision or requirement number it can see plus one, so two branches take the same number and the second to land is renumbered by hand after a conflict; this specification's own history holds ten such renumbering commits, and nothing in the design said how parallel branches should take an ID.

Cause: omitted (the specification left it out).

Affects: adds `#/decisions/ADR-238`.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-04. ADR-238 is recorded as proposed: it weighs a provisional name rewritten at landing, a specarch renumber command and IDs that cannot clash against a reservation counter, and recommends the counter with one option on specarch decide (--id). It is not built: the ID patterns, both validator builds, the commands and docs/conventions.md are unchanged, so no file's output, error or exit status changes and the release takes it as a patch-sized entry.

Released in 1.5.0.

### CR-43: Refuse an approval by a role never heard, and name the session, test session or communication record in which the documents were read

Raised by specification-author on 2026-11-04, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

approve accepted any stakeholder, so a role nobody had ever talked to could approve the documents and be the first to object at acceptance, and an approval record did not say where, or with whom, the documents were read.

Affects: adds `#/decisions/ADR-239`, `#/requirements/SA-133`, `#/tests/approve-refuses-session-absent`, `#/tests/approve-refuses-session-missing`, `#/tests/approve-refuses-unheard`, `#/tests/approve-warns-no-session`, `#/tests/validate-approval-session`; changes `#/commands/approve`, `#/enums/Rule`, `#/tests/approve-after-document-records-and-site`, `#/tests/approve-refuses-stale-document`, `#/tests/approve-stakeholders-complete`, `#/tests/approve-warns-stakeholders-unconfirmed`, `#/tests/approve-writes-record`.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-05. approve refuses, with exit 1, a --by role that no communication, session, test session, interview or decision names, the same definition of heard as the rule unheard; --session names the record in which the role read the documents and is written into the approval record, a record that does not list the role is the new error approval_session, and approve without --session warns and still writes the record (ADR-239, SA-133). This is a break: specarch approve --by a role never heard exited 0 and wrote the record on 1.5.0, and exits 1 now, so specarch diff asks for 2.0.0. The owner decided on 2026-11-05 to release it as 1.6.0, a minor step, as for the record schema's cause in 1.5.0 (CR-27). No specification file clean on 1.5.0 gets a new error: validate on v1.5.0's own tree gives 0 errors with this build.

Released in 1.6.0.

### CR-46: Read tables from a tagged PDF's structure tree, and refuse a PDF with no text layer

Raised by specification-author on 2026-11-04, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

The PDF reader read a table by the position of its text, so a table in a tagged PDF came out as loose lines and lost its rows; a scanned PDF with no text layer gave one could question per page instead of saying it cannot be read; and a page the page tree counted but held no page for was silently skipped.

Cause: omitted (the specification left it out).

Affects: adds `#/tests/extract-documents-pdf-markdown-twin`, `#/tests/extract-documents-pdf-no-text`, `#/tests/extract-documents-pdf-tagged`, `#/tests/extract-documents-pdf-untagged`; changes `#/commands/extract`, `#/decisions/ADR-212`, `#/requirements/SA-110`.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-05. extract documents reads the tables of a tagged PDF from its structure tree, keeping a table's continuation on the next page and bounding the walk by a budget counted on every entry it reads; a PDF none of whose pages holds text is refused with status 1 as a scanned document with no text layer, a page with no page object is a line naming it, and a PDF gives the requirements and questions its Markdown twin gives (ADR-212, SA-110). Raised by specification-author on 2026-11-05, in development. Additive, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-05. Intent phase 1 (ADR-244, SA-135 to SA-139): problem, goals, outOfScope and qualityGoals are optional requirements-stage keys of the 1.0 schemas; validate warns problem_missing, goal_unmeasured, goal_unserved, need_without_goal, scope_conflict and quality_goal_rank, gated as stakeholders_unconfirmed is; document intent writes intent.md and the techspec, traceability and progress documents show the intent where it is stated; gaps --next asks for the intent first; init takes --problem, --goal and --out-of-scope and, on a terminal with none given, asks the three questions. ### CR-54: Fail specarch diff's version check when a specification keeps the version of a released one

Raised by specification-author on 2026-11-05, in development. Perfective, normal urgency; impact minor. Status: released.

When both folders carried the same info.version, diff left the version check out for any version, a released one too, so a release whose info.version never stepped passed the version step and shipped under the number of the release before it (BUG-075).

Cause: wrong (the specification said it wrongly).

Affects: adds `#/tests/diff-same-version-planned`, `#/tests/diff-same-version-released`, `#/tests/diff-same-version-released-unchanged`; changes `#/commands/diff`, `#/decisions/ADR-224`.

Decision: approved by specification-author on 2026-11-06. In the same-version case diff reads the release record beside the old folder, and when that exact version is released it reports error: version: naming the record and the version to step to, and exits 1; a version not yet released, compared with itself, keeps only the coverage check (ADR-224). specarch diff rates the new path diff reads as a major change, and a run that exited 0 on 1.6.0 for a released version kept unchanged exits 1 now. That run passed only because of the bug: it is the outcome the design of diff always asked for, and no correct release relied on it. The owner decided on 2026-11-06 to release it in 1.7.0, a minor step, as for 1.6.0 (CR-51).

Released in 1.7.0.
